newsitem.title: USA: US rail container freight volume at new record - AAR.
newsitem.headline: US rail container freight volume at new record - AAR.

text.p: Container freight volume on the nation's railroads broke all previous records in the week ended June 14, the Association of American Railroads said Thursday.
AAR reported 103,554 containers, up 2.8 percent from the previous record of 100,726 in the week ended September 28, 1996.

It also reported 67,185 trailers in the week, bringing total intermodal volume to 170,739 trailers and containers, up 7.2 percent from 159,212 in the same 1996 week. Intermodal does not include carloads.
But carload freight, which does not include intermodal, fell 1.9 percent in the June 14 week to 348,591 carloads from 355,245 a year ago.
Ton-miles in the week also declined 1.5 percent to 26.4 billion from 26.8 billion a year ago. The ton-mile, a measure of freight transportation, is one ton of freight hauled one mile.
AAR attributed the 1.9 percent decrease in carloads last week to a 6.7 percent decline in coal loadings, which totalled 129,644 in the June 14 week compared with 138,918 a year ago.
AAR said the drop in coal loadings offset a 7.1 percent rise in carloads of grain, which stood at 23,207 in the week compared with 21,670 in the year-ago week.
AAR also reported declines in carloads of metallic ores, which fell 4.5 percent to 21,494 from 22,506 last year, and in primary forest products, down four percent to 7,291 loadings from 7,592.

But there were increases in carloads of farm products other than grain, which rose 14.2 percent to 1,871 carloads last week from 1,639 a year ago, and in nonmetallic minerals, up five percent to 9,611 carloads from 9,153 in the year-ago week, AAR said.
Petroleum products also rose 4.5 percent to 5,799 carloads from 5,550, AAR said.

AAR said carloads on the two Canadian-based U.S. railroads rose sharply from a year ago, up 9.8 percent to 54,583 carloads in the June 14 week, while intermodal traffic climbed 11.6 percent to 24,827 trailers and containers.

In the first 24 weeks of 1997, AAR said carloads increased 1.5 percent to 8.15 million from 8.03 million in the same 1996 period. Trailers and containers rose 6.7 percent to 3.89 million from 3.64 million, while ton-miles increased two percent in the period to 635.0 billion from 622.6 billion.

For the same period, AAR reported 1.27 million carloads on the two Canadian-based U.S. railroads, up 1.8 percent from the year-ago period, and 582,985 trailers and containers, up 11.2 percent from last year, AAR said.

Combined total volume in the United States and Canada for the first 24 weeks was 9.42 million carloads, up 1.5 percent from the same 1996 period, while intermodal traffic totaled 4.47 million trailers and containers, up 7.2 percent from last year, AAR said.
